name: Ponosakan
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand descriptions agree (0 state the same rule, 1 refine it); none contradicts.

new_statements.quote: Di dalam bahasa (dialek) Ponosakan tidak ditemukan pasangan-pasangan kata yang menunjukkan kehadiran tekanan yang bersifat distintif. [...] Salah satu hal yang nyata dalam pemakaian tekanan kata para penutur bahasa (dialek) Ponosakan ialah penempatan tekanan kata yang agak kurang konsisten. [...] kata-kata yang bersuku kata dua, ada yang tekanan kata dijatuhkan pada suku kata akhir dan ada pula pada suku kata kedua dari akhir. [...] (1) bahasa (dialek) Ponosakan mempunyai tekanan kata ultima atau penultima; [...] (3) pada umumnya kata dasar yang bersuku kata dua dengan suku kata akhir terbuka, tekanan kata jatuh pada suku kata akhir.
new_statements.translation: In the Ponosakan language (dialect) no word pairs were found that show the presence of distinctive stress. [...] One evident fact in the use of word stress by Ponosakan speakers is that the placement of word stress is rather inconsistent. [...] in disyllabic words, some have word stress placed on the final syllable and some on the second syllable from the end. [...] (1) Ponosakan has ultimate or penultimate word stress; [...] (3) in general, in disyllabic root words with an open final syllable, word stress falls on the final syllable. (P. 66 summary adds: 'Bahasa (dialek) Ponosakan tidak memiliki tekanan kata yang berfungsi distingtif. Keragaman pemakaian tekanan kata yang nyata sekarang adalah peralihan dari ultima ke penultima atau sebaliknya yang terjadi (secara hipotetis).' = Ponosakan has no distinctively functioning word stress; the present variation in stress usage is (hypothetically) a transition from ultima to penultima or the reverse.)
new_statements.citation: Danie, J. Akun, F. Rogi-Warouw, A.B.G. Rattu & G. Karim Bachmid. 1991. Fonologi bahasa Ponosokan. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Departemen Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan. viii+154 pp. ISBN 9794591173.

new_statements.relation_note: Catalog codes Ponosakan as fixed final (final stress, an earlier compilation-2026-08-31, evidently from Lobel 2016: 'stress is not contrastive.. regularly falls on word-final syllables, with a few unpredictable exceptions where it falls on the penultimate'). Danie et al. agree that stress is non-contrastive and that final stress is the general case at least for open-final disyllabic roots, and they add an alternating secondary-stress pattern; but they do NOT commit to a single fixed position, describing placement as 'agak kurang konsisten' between ultima and penult and hypothesising a shift in progress. Compatible with the catalog's final coding but weaker: it documents more final~penult va…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is not contrastive (no minimal pairs; speakers confirm stress never distinguishes meaning). Placement is inconsistent: in disyllables (and likewise tri- and quadrisyllables) stress is heard sometimes on the final syllable, sometimes on the penult; the authors say this makes the system hard to determine and offer only hypotheses: (1) stress is ultimate or penultimate, (2) the variation reflects an ongoing shift ultima->penult or penult->ultima, (3) disyllabic roots with an open final syllable generally carry final stress. Stress is marked (') in the phonetic transcriptions of sections 3.2-3.3, and the long vowel allophones [i:, a:, u:] are described as occurring in open, stressed final syllables.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Alternating rhythm reported (p. 61-62): in trisyllables, when stress falls on the final syllable the third-from-last syllable is also stressed; when the penult is stressed, the final and antepenultimate syllables are unstressed; in four-syllable words stress 'varies between the odd-numbered syllables from the end and each even-numbered syllable from the end' (i.e. alternate syllables counting from whichever of ultima/penult carries stress).
new_statements.exceptions: No lexical exception list; the variation itself (final vs penult tokens in words of every length) is the reported irregularity. Hypothesis (3) restricts the 'generally final' statement to disyllabic roots whose final syllable is open. Loanword adaptation (3.8) says nothing about stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Danie et al. 1991 describe Ponosakan ('bahasa (dialek) Ponosakan/Ponosokan', treated as an old dialect of Mongondow) as spoken in Kecamatan Belang, southeastern Minahasa, North Sulawesi; primary data from an elderly main informant plus 2-3 supporting informants in kelurahan Buku (Belang), with Tababo and Gorgo also visited; c. 2,000 speakers reported at the time. Same variety as Lobel 2016 (Belang). The scan runs to printed p. 96 plus appendices (113 PDF pages), fewer than the viii+154 pp of the bibliographic record, but the phonology chapters, conclusions and bibliography are complete.

readall_conflicts: No outright contradiction, but a difference of degree: Lobel 2016 (LD&C 10, p. 399; the basis of the catalog's fixed: final syllable record) says non-contrastive stress 'regularly falls on word-final syllables, with a few unpredictable exceptions' on the penult, whereas Danie, Rogi-Warouw, Rattu & Bachmid 1991 (pp. 61-62, 66) find placement 'rather inconsistent' between ultima and penult in words of all lengths, decline to fix a single system, and only hypothesise 'ultima atau penultima' stress with final stress as the general case for disyllabic roots with an open final syllable, plus a possible ultima<->penult shift in progress. Both agree stress is not distinctive. The catalog's final coding stands, best read as 'non-contrastive, predominantly final, with penult variants'.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant', final stress (final stress, not in the strict set) matches Lobel 2016 exactly: stress non-contrastive, regularly word-final, a few unpredictable penultimate exceptions. The quotation is verified verbatim at p. 399 of the open LD&C PDF (now, identical to the Aug-31 scan copy). The source is first-hand and modern (the documenter of the last speakers), so nothing suggests the classification is wrong; but the record's cite/loc/grade fields are blank and the catalog 'held' list is empty, so the action is to register the copy consulted, add locator 'p. 399', and set an strength of the evidence. sources.quote: As in other Mongondow-Gorontalo languages, stress is not contrastive in Ponosakan, and regularly falls on word-final syllables, with a few unpredictable exceptions where it falls on the penultimate syllable, e.g., si'ene [si'?ene] 'who'.
